title: Thermodynamics of Gas Turbines & Heat Cycles

content.objective: To evaluate the thermal efficiency and specific fuel consumption of a small-scale Brayton cycle gas turbine under variable load conditions.
content.theory: The ideal Brayton cycle consists of isentropic compression in the compressor, isobaric heat addition in the combustion chamber, isentropic expansion in the turbine, and isobaric heat rejection.
procedure: Perform pre-run oil pressure and fuel line checks on the turbine bench.
Start the gas turbine and allow the exhaust gas temperature (EGT) to stabilize at idle.
Gradually increase electrical dynamometer load from 0.5 kW to 2.5 kW in 0.5 kW steps.
Record compressor inlet/outlet pressures, turbine inlet temperature, and mass flow rate of fuel.
content.conclusion: Thermal efficiency increased with higher pressure ratios, reaching a peak of 18.7% at maximum rated turbine shaft output.
